Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Learned A.G.A. has informed that notice to the informant has been served on 11.02.2025.
3. Second supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.

4. Heard Sri Sunil Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri V.K.S. Parmar,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
5. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.160 of 2024, under Sections 328, 109, 366A, 376(3) I.P.C.
& 5t/6 POCSO Act, Police Station Titawi, District Muzaffarnagar, during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.

Learned counsel has further stated that the prosecution witnesses i.e. P.W.1 is the informant, P.W.2 is the eye witness and P.W.3 is the victim, have not supported the prosecution story and they have turned hostile.
There is no likelihood of conviction of the applicant in the present case.
The witnesses have been cross-examined by the public prosecutor.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 13.07.2024.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
7. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application but could not dispute the fact that there is no criminal history of the applicant and the witnesses have turned hostile.
8. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

9. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.
The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
11.
Learned AGA could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
12. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA.

13. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

14. Let the applicant- Satyam Kumar, involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Satyam Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158459706/
2 court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

entities.text: Satyam Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
15. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

16. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
